question.text: In Young's double-slit experiment, the distance between slits and the screen is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> and monochromatic light of wavelength <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>600</mn><mo> </mo><mi>nm</mi></math> is being used. A person standing near the slits is looking at the fringe pattern. When the separation between the slits is varied, the interference pattern disappears for a particular distance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>d</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></math> between the slits. If the angular resolution of the eye is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>60</mn></mfrac><mo>°</mo></math>, then the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>d</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></math> is close to

solution.text:
When the angular fringe width in the interference pattern becomes less than the angular resolving power of the person's eye, the fringes will disappear.

The angular fringe width θ 0 = β D = λ d 0

d 0 = λ θ 0 = 600× 10 −9 ( 1 60 × π 180 )

d0=600×60×180×10−9π m=2 mm
